title: Zero Re-render Form State Engine (React Hook Form Core)
concept: Uncontrolled Refs with Event Subscriptions for High-Performance Forms
problemStatement: Implement `createFormEngine(initialValues)` that registers input fields via refs, tracks touched and dirty states, validates fields without re-rendering parent components, and returns serialized values on submit.
interviewTrap: Storing form values in top-level useState forces the entire form component tree to re-render on every keystroke. Using uncontrolled ref-based subscription isolated to inputs scales to thousands of inputs smoothly.

testCases.name: Updates field value on change without external rerenders
testCases.testFn: const form = createFormEngine(); const emailField = form.register('email'); emailField.onChange('alex@test.com'); return form.getValues();

testCases.name: Validates field and records error message
testCases.testFn: const form = createFormEngine(); const pass = form.register('password', val => val.length < 8 ? 'Too short' : null); pass.onChange('123'); return form.getErrors();

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does React Hook Form achieve zero-rerender form typing performance?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: React Hook Form uses **Uncontrolled Components with Mutable Refs**! When a user types into an input registered via `register('email')`, React does NOT call `setState` and does NOT re-render the form. The DOM node updates natively at 60fps. React Hook Form listens to native DOM `input` events, updates an internal in-memory object ref, and only triggers targeted re-renders on components that explicitly subscribe via `useWatch` or when validation errors occur.

realWorldUseCases.description: Complex insurance or medical forms with hundreds of fields where controlled state causes typing lag.

howToExplain.opening: React Hook Form achieves zero re-renders during typing by embracing uncontrolled DOM inputs and managing state in mutable refs with isolated subscriptions.
keyPoints: Controlled forms re-render the entire component on every keystroke.
Uncontrolled inputs update natively in the browser DOM.
Refs capture values without triggering React render passes.
Subscriptions (useWatch) selectively re-render only dependent fields.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Bypassing React re-renders for high-frequency typing is why React Hook Form outperformed Formik and Redux Form.
analogies: Directly writing notes on a physical paper form instead of dictating every letter over the phone to someone typing in another room.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using watch() at the top-level form component in React Hook Form.
commonMistakes.why: Calling watch() without arguments forces the entire form to re-render on every keystroke, destroying the zero-rerender advantage.
commonMistakes.correct: Use useWatch() in isolated child components.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React Hook Form integrate with schema validators like Zod?
followUpDeepDive.answer: It uses a `resolver` wrapper (`@hookform/resolvers/zod`): on submit or blur, it passes the form ref data to `zodSchema.safeParseAsync()`, mapping validation issues to form error states.
